raw_review_excerpt:
The diagnostic correctly maps the code paths that produce the failure: Codex provider concatenates agent_message text (provider.ts:329), tries JSON.parse on the full accumulation (provider.ts:482), and the executor fallback parseStructuredOutputText (dag-executor.ts:2106) also uses a single JSON.parse. Both paths reject concatenated JSON, so the typed decision gate never fires and the sentinel is never emitted. However, the fix recommendation (Option A deduplication) is undergrounded — the actual shape of the failing accumulatedText is inferred, not observed, and a simpler structural fix (stop accumulating multiple complete agent_messages into one string) is never considered.

Issues:
- 1. [WARN] Fix selection based on inferred, not observed, input shape
- 2. [WARN] Simpler structural alternative not considered: last-complete-message wins
- 3. [WARN] Open Question 1 is a gating precondition, not a follow-up
- 4. [NOTE] Prompt coherence between typed decision contract and sentinel contract

issues.title: Fix selection based on inferred, not observed, input shape
issues.details: The diagnostic concludes the accumulatedText is duplicated identical JSON (e.g. {"decision":"advance"}{"decision":"advance"}) but never quotes the actual provider log payload from run 127b99692faf196c633ea1c4d9aec649. The codex.structured_output_not_json warning includes an outputPreview field (provider.ts:486) that would show the exact bytes. Without it, the recommended dedup fix may target the wrong shape — the real payload could be thinking-text + JSON, two different JSON objects from session replay, or JSON inside markdown fences plus bare JSON.
issues.suggested_fix: Before committing to a fix approach, retrieve the actual outputPreview from the codex.structured_output_not_json log entry for this run. The shape of the bytes determines which fix is correct.

issues.title: Simpler structural alternative not considered: last-complete-message wins
issues.details: The Codex provider accumulates ALL agent_message item.text into accumulatedText (provider.ts:329). But Codex items arrive as item.completed events with complete text payloads (provider.ts:312-328). When output_format requests a single JSON object, accumulating multiple complete agent_messages is itself the design error — concatenating any two complete messages produces invalid JSON whether they're identical or not. A 'last complete agent_message wins' approach would handle identical duplicates, thinking-then-result patterns, and session replay artifacts without making JSON parsing more lenient.
issues.suggested_fix: Add Option D: for output_format turns, track the last agent_message item.text separately and use it as the structured output candidate instead of accumulating all messages. This addresses the structural cause rather than patching the symptom.

issues.title: Open Question 1 is a gating precondition, not a follow-up
issues.details: The diagnostic lists 'Does the Codex SDK intentionally emit multiple agent_message chunks for the same output-format turn?' as an open question. But this question determines whether deduplication is the right fix or whether Archon is seeing replayed/resumed messages due to a session handling bug. If the latter, dedup masks a state bug that will manifest differently elsewhere.
issues.suggested_fix: Promote this from Open Questions to a required investigation step before fix selection. Check Codex SDK documentation and/or instrument the provider to log each item.completed event's item.id to determine if the messages are genuinely distinct items or replayed.

issues.title: Prompt coherence between typed decision contract and sentinel contract
issues.details: The YAML prompt (lines 839-852) has two competing signal contracts: the sentinel emission contract (emit <promise>PLANNING_REVIEW_APPROVED</promise>) and the typed decision contract (set decision to advance). The diagnostic correctly identifies this duality but frames Option C (prompt hardening) as a symptom-only fix. However, the prompt incoherence is a real issue independent of the runtime bug — the model prioritized the typed contract and skipped the sentinel, which is rational behavior given the prompt structure. Even after fixing the runtime, this dual-signal confusion wastes tokens and creates fragile gate behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Regardless of which runtime fix ships, clean up the prompt to make the typed decision gate primary and demote the sentinel to an explicit fallback clause rather than a co-equal requirement. This is a follow-up, not a blocker for the runtime fix.

review.best_case: The code path analysis is correct, the runtime does have a real gap in handling multi-message structured output, and Option A (provider-side normalization) would fix the observed failure if the accumulatedText shape is indeed duplicated identical JSON. The diagnostic correctly identifies the two-mechanism completion system as the architectural context and correctly prioritizes a runtime fix over prompt churn.
strongest_objections: The fix targets an inferred input shape — the actual accumulatedText was never inspected. If the real payload is thinking-text-plus-JSON or session-replay artifacts rather than identical duplicates, the deep-equality dedup in Option A will fail-stop and the bug persists.

A simpler structural fix exists: stop accumulating multiple complete agent_messages and instead use the last complete message. This handles all realistic duplication shapes without making JSON parsing more lenient, and it's absent from the options list.

Open Question 1 (is duplication intentional SDK behavior or a session bug?) is a precondition for fix selection, not a follow-up. Committing to dedup before answering it risks masking a state management bug.
hidden_assumptions: The diagnostic assumes all agent_message items in a Codex output-format turn carry the same text (identical duplication). Real-world Codex behavior may produce thinking/reasoning as agent_message items before the final structured response.

The diagnostic assumes the provider's accumulatedText is the only source of the problem, but doesn't consider whether Codex session resume/replay could produce the duplication — in which case the bug is in session handling, not in JSON parsing.

Option A's 'deeply equal → keep one' logic assumes the dedup case is the common case. If most real failures involve non-identical payloads, the fail-stop path preserves the original failure mode and the fix has no practical effect.

The recommendation assumes the executor's parseStructuredOutputText fallback (line 2614) sees the same concatenated text as the provider. In practice, fullOutput comes from assistant chunks (line 2408), which may include interleaved tool output and thinking, making it even harder to parse as JSON.
review.what_would_change_my_mind: If the actual outputPreview from the failing run's log shows literally duplicated identical JSON (e.g. {"decision":"advance"}{"decision":"advance"} with no interleaving), then Option A is well-targeted. If Codex SDK documentation confirms that multiple agent_message items per turn is expected behavior for output-format turns, then provider-side normalization is the right layer. Both of these are retrievable facts that the diagnostic should have grounded before recommending a fix.
